(Nov 24): Indonesia said a recent decline in natural gas flows to Singapore was due to pipeline maintenance, moving the focus away from its rising domestic needs.

“There were pipeline repairs previously — we did reduce supply,” Energy and Mineral Resources Minister Bahlil Lahadalia told reporters after a press conference on Monday. “We have to honour a contract.”

Indonesia reduced gas exports to Singapore for more than two weeks from Oct 24, as Indonesia President Prabowo Subianto stressed the importance of safeguarding the exporter’s natural resources and prioritising domestic needs. That came as a regional haze because of forest fires, which added to tensions between the nations.

Indonesia also commissioned a pipeline connection allowing gas from Natuna, which had previously flowed to Singapore, to be diverted to power plants in Batam. The cut did not breach contracts, as Indonesia would still meet its minimum deliveries, Bahlil said last month.

Indonesia fully restored gas flows to Singapore on Nov 12 and there has been no further notification of supply reduction, the city-state’s Ministry of Energy, Trade and Industry said last week.

Tensions between the neighbours have eased recently, with Prabowo apologising to Singapore and Malaysia earlier this month for the haze that blanketed parts of Southeast Asia. That followed a visit by Singapore Foreign Minister Vivian Balakrishnan to Indonesia last month, which resulted in the formation of a joint task force to tackle forest fires.

See also: Oil extends decline on signs of continuing US-Iran diplomacy

title: Rakuten Group shelves bond sale of up to ¥151 bil
article:
(Nov 24): Rakuten Group Inc has cancelled a planned bond sale of as much as ¥151 billion, according to an emailed statement from Goldman Sachs, one of the deal’s arrangers.

Goldman Sachs said the cancellation was at the issuer’s request. Rakuten Group shares fell as much as 3.9% to their lowest intraday level since November 2023.

Its yen bond spreads widened last week after a potential customer-data leak at a group brokerage. Rakuten Securities Inc said on Nov 17 that client data including names, addresses, annual income and financial assets may have been leaked from as many as 4.47 million accounts.

Rakuten has repeatedly tapped domestic and overseas bond markets to meet its large funding needs, as its mobile business continues to post heavy losses. Wider spreads on its yen debt could make future borrowing more expensive.

The spread on ¥360 billion of bonds it sold to individuals in October widened to about 220 basis points over Japanese government debt as of Nov 20, the highest since issuance.

Rakuten Group said last week that it received an order from Japan’s Financial Services Agency to submit a report under the Financial Instruments and Exchange Act following the possible data leak at Rakuten Securities.

See also: Tech companies are getting more creative to raise billions

A Rakuten Group spokesperson said the timing of its next bond issue has yet to be determined. The person declined to comment on whether the data-leak issue had affected its sale plans.

title: Malaysia tells data centres to cut off firms on US blacklist
article:
(Nov 24): Malaysia will advise data centre operators not to host, lease space or provide services to seven companies newly placed on a US trade blacklist, stepping up efforts to prevent the country’s booming industry from being used to circumvent American technology restrictions.

“Malaysia remains committed to a secure, transparent and rules-based trading environment and will not allow itself to be used as a channel to circumvent export controls,” the Ministry of Investment, Trade and Industry said in a statement on Tuesday. “Action will be taken against parties found to have contravened any laws.”

The US commerce department on Monday added Megaspeed International — the firm at the heart of a scandal that briefly cost Jensen Huang his job as Nvidia Corp chief executive officer — and six other companies in Southeast Asia to its trade blacklist, barring them from buying high-end AI chips and other advanced technology without a US government licence.

Malaysia’s trade ministry said only two of the entities — Speedmatrix Sdn Bhd and MSFusion Sdn Bhd — are listed under the country. Speedmatrix is a wholly owned subsidiary of Singapore-based Megaspeed International.

The US action intensifies scrutiny of Malaysia’s rapidly expanding data centre industry as Washington seeks to prevent advanced artificial intelligence chips from reaching restricted users, particularly through third countries. Malaysia has emerged as a major destination for data centre investment amid surging demand for computing capacity to support artificial intelligence services.

Revelations about Jensen Huang’s alleged affair with Megaspeed’s former CEO, Alice Huang, who has been accused of spying for China, have put fresh scrutiny on allegations that the firm helped smuggle Nvidia’s artificial intelligence chips into China.

See also: Why Khazanah is looking to Malaysia's mid term firms for growth

title: US Thanksgiving air travel to hit 16-year high, testing reliability
article:
(Nov 24): Thanksgiving air travel in the US is set to reach a 16-year high as millions of people take to the skies, in a major test of aviation safety and reliability after this month’s nationwide outage.

More than 417,000 flights are scheduled during the nine-day holiday period, the Department of Transportation said in a statement Monday. Tuesday, Nov 25, is forecast to be the busiest day with more than 52,000 flights. Last year, over 360,000 services were scheduled over the Thanksgiving holiday.

The US government is seeking to reassure travellers after the industry was hit by a series of technology issues this month. In the worst case, an air traffic control tech outage led to a rare nationwide grounding of US flights, with around 20,000 services being cancelled. Just days later, a tech failure caused a four-hour outage at United Airlines Holdings Inc. This week, Delta Air Lines Inc briefly halted departures at its Atlanta hub Sunday after a technology outage triggered delays and cancellations.

“The Trump Administration’s message is clear: your safety is our number one priority,” Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said in a statement. “The American people can rest assured we will continue to work around the clock 24/7 to get families where they need to go.”

Duffy has called for US$50 billion in emergency funding to fix decades-old air traffic equipment.

title: China stockpiles soyoil as domestic prices hit three-month low
article:
(Nov 24): China is stepping up purchases of soybean oil for state reserves to help soak up a domestic glut, as heavy soybean crushing boosts production while demand for the cooking oil struggles to keep pace.

State stockpiler Sinograin will seek offers on Wednesday for another 200,000 tonnes of soyoil, marking the fourth purchase in the latest round of tenders, it said late last week. The state-run firm has secured about a third of the 600,000 tonnes targeted for reserves in tenders so far this month, according to China-based consultancy Mysteel.

Crushers have been processing massive volumes of soybeans, churning out ample supplies of meal for livestock feed and oil for cooking. But soyoil consumption remains subdued heading into peak demand season ahead of the Lunar New Year, weighed down by a slowing economy and shrinking population.

Spot prices for soy oil in Shandong, a key processing hub, and futures on the Dalian Commodity Exchange have both fallen to the lowest since early August.

The glut comes as China receives large quantities of soybeans from both Brazil and the US. State-owned buyers have purchased American shipments to help Beijing meet a target of at least 25 million tonnes annually through 2028. While much of that is expected to enter state reserves, some stockpiled beans have been released onto the market to make room for incoming supplies. Private crushers, meanwhile, have snapped up Brazilian beans, adding to the oversupply.

See also: Papua New Guinea clan chiefs seek to block massive copper mine

US President Donald Trump said on Monday he will announce a trade deal involving large purchases of soybeans, days after the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen where he met Chinese President Xi Jinping. He did not specify from which country but made the comments after referencing the US trading relationship with China.

Chinese soybean imports in the first ten months of the year hit 93.5 million tonnes, a comparable level to the previous year. Traders expect arrivals in November and December at more than nine million tonnes each, higher than a year earlier.

At the same time, edible oil consumption in the country is falling, according to a US Department of Agriculture report this month that cited reduced dining out, rising health consciousness, and an ageing and declining population.

See also: Copper falls below US$12,000 in London as metals turmoil deepens

Commercial inventories of soy oil in key Chinese regions have risen to their highest since at least 2024, according to Mysteel.

title: Bitcoin fails to hold Nvidia bump with crypto headwinds in focus
article:
(Nov 24): Bitcoin failed to sustain its rally even as global stocks soared on the news of Jensen Huang’s reinstatement as CEO of Nvidia Corp, with investors focusing on the headwinds facing cryptocurrencies.

The largest digital asset weakened as much as 3% to US$59,404 in Asia on Tuesday (Nov 24) after fully erasing its nearly 6% jump on the Nvidia announcement during the US session. Bitcoin, which sank to a two-year low of US$55,254 over the weekend, has fallen about 20% in November.

The US$6 billion hack of Binance on Oct 29 knocked confidence in crypto markets, while outflows from US spot bitcoin exchange-traded funds have accelerated, removing a key source of price support. While Huang’s return sent stock markets surging, the rebound in risk assets also reinforced expectations that the Federal Reserve has room to raise interest rates, a potential negative for non-yielding assets such as bitcoin.

“The Jensen rally was not as bullish a catalyst for bitcoin, as the rally in risk will make it easier for the Fed to hike in December,” said Rich Rosenblum, co-founder of crypto market maker GSR.

Bitcoin has lost more than half its value since reaching a peak above US$126,000 in October 2025. The token notched its seventh straight weekly decline last week, with the liquidation of leveraged long positions quickening its slump.

See also: Bitcoin ETF exodus gathers pace, removing key source of support

Democrats winning US midterm elections on Nov 3 raised expectations of greater regulatory scrutiny of the crypto industry when they retake both chambers of Congress next year.

Outflows from US-listed bitcoin ETFs have gathered pace, with about US$1.8 billion drained last week, the most since June. Some US$4.8 billion has been pulled since Oct 30, according to data compiled by Bloomberg.

Bitcoin’s price retreat may soon start to make it enticing, said Alex Kuptsikevich, chief market analyst at FxPro.

See also: Bitcoin extends reversal from Trump election gain to hit below US$56,000

“Current levels could present a welcome second chance for long-term purchases and offer a favourable risk-reward ratio for speculators,” he said. “However, cautious investors will likely prefer to wait for signs of a reversal, such as a recovery above the 200-week moving average, which currently stands at US$68,200.”

title: Oil extends decline on signs of continuing US-Iran diplomacy
article:
(Nov 24): Oil pushed lower after sliding more than 3% in the previous session on cautious optimism over efforts to end the US-Iran war.

Brent crude traded around US$89 a barrel, while West Texas Intermediate slipped below US$80. Vice-President JD Vance met with Qatar’s prime minister to discuss negotiations with Iran, according to Axios. The Persian Gulf nation has acted as a mediator in efforts to resolve the near nine-month conflict.

Global benchmark Brent has tumbled this month after US President Donald Trump held off on renewed strikes following the Democratic sweep of US midterm elections, although there has been an increase in low-level fighting. Trump recently threatened to resume attacks next year if talks fail.

Despite the hostilities, including frequent attacks on tankers transiting the Strait of Hormuz, crude exports from the Persian Gulf have surged. The International Energy Agency predicts the market will swing to a surplus this quarter, while Goldman Sachs Group Inc has flagged a possible glut next year.

“Supply-demand dynamics and the geopolitical winds are both blowing in a bearish direction,” said Robert Yawger, director of the energy futures division at Mizuho Securities USA LLC.

While there is some hope of a negotiated settlement, major differences between the two sides remain. Tehran wants a US naval blockade of its ports lifted, sanctions eased and frozen assets released before fully reopening Hormuz. Washington is demanding concessions related to Iran’s nuclear programme.

See also: US Senate probes Vance role in Vitol choice for Venezuela oil

title: Seatrium to retrench 2% of Singapore workforce
article:
Mainboard-listed Seatrium has announced that it is laying off around 220 employees, or 2% of its Singapore workforce on Nov 24. The move is part of its overall business restructuring plan to position the company for “long-term resilience and growth”.

The announcement comes after Seatrium forecasted stronger y-o-y earnings for FY2026 on Nov 19.

Seatrium says that the employees are offered retrenchment packages in line with the Tripartite Advisory on Managing Excess Manpower and Responsible Retrenchment. According to the advisory, the prevailing norm is to pay a retrenchment benefit varying between 2 weeks to one month salary per year of service, depending on the financial position of the company and taking into consideration the industry norm.

In unionised companies where the quantum of retrenchment benefit is stipulated in the collective agreement, the norm is one month salary for each year of service. Employees with 2 years’ service or more are eligible for retrenchment benefit while those with less than 2 years’ service could be granted an ex-gratia payment.

Seatrium will be undertaking the exercise, called the Workforce Redesign Programme, with its house union Seatrium Employees Union (SEU). The programme aims to deliver a more “integrated and future-ready” operating model and comprises the optimisation of Singapore operations and workforce restructuring.

When asked if this was the only round of job cuts, Seatrium replied, “As an operating company, Seatrium will continue to assess its resource requirements in line with its business and project needs.”

See also: Metrocon to resume trading on Sept 15 after RTO

Prior to undertaking this exercise, Seatrium says that it has reviewed redeployment opportunities, workforce upskilling initiatives and other workforce optimisation measures. These include investing nearly $7 million in employee training in FY2025 and over 600,000 training hours globally across technical, leadership and capability-building programmes.

However, due to the “rapid pace” of changes in its operating environment and the streamlining of its footprint, some roles are no longer aligned with Seatrium’s business model and structure, says the company.

This is Seatrium’s first workforce restructuring exercise as it aims to redesign its workforce to support changing business demands. These changes are distinct from the usual workforce movements that routinely evolve according to project lifecycles, mobilisation requirements and workload demands.

See also: Hatten Land lodges circular for $28 mil RTO of Metrocon

Seatrium CEO Chris Ong says: “Our people have been instrumental in building Seatrium into the global business it is today, and we are deeply grateful for every colleague’s contributions over the past 60 years. We are not downsizing or simply cost cutting.

"We are repositioning and readying Seatrium to capture new opportunities, ensuring we have the right capabilities, skills and operating models to compete in a rapidly evolving industry and support our ambitions. While these decisions are difficult, and the transition will not be straightforward, I am confident Seatrium’s proven tenacity will ensure we emerge stronger.”

Seatrium says that it had notified SEU, a newly formed house union of Seatrium, in advance of the exercise and assured that all alternative options for the affected employees had been explored.

The SEU says that it worked to ensure that affected employees were treated fairly and the retrenchment packages are in line with the Tripartite Advisory on Managing Excess Manpower and Responsible Retrenchment.

SEU president Atyyah Bti Hassan says: “Workforce transitions are never easy. SEU was engaged early in the process and worked closely with the company throughout the exercise. Outplacement support will be provided by Seatrium and the Union to all affected employees, and SEU’s priority will be to safeguard the interests of affected employees and strengthen the support available to them.”

title: Papua New Guinea clan chiefs seek to block massive copper mine
article:
(Nov 24): Traditional landowners in Papua New Guinea are seeking to block development of a giant copper mine that has been closed for almost 40 years and was once a flash point in a brutal civil war, saying they are its true owners under a regional constitution.

Beverly Bakaori, chief of the Bakoringku clan, is challenging the legality of the granting of a 25-year mining lease for the Panguna deposit to parties including India’s Lloyds Metals & Energy Ltd, according to an emailed statement from Numa Numa Resources Inc, a closely held company that has backing from local landowners. She has sought an injunction to prevent Lloyds and the Autonomous Bougainville Government from progressing mining and to hand over control of the vast copper and gold deposit.

Lloyds did not immediately reply to a request for comment during a holiday in India. The ABG, as the government is known, did not immediately reply to an email.

Panguna was closed down in 1989 under the ownership of Rio Tinto Group due to local protests over environmental damage and revenue distribution, which degenerated into a civil conflict that killed as many as 20,000 people. The mine’s remaining reserves are estimated at 5.3 million tonnes of copper and 19.3 million ounces of gold, worth more than US$130 billion at current prices.

Bakaori represents five regional clans, as well as Panguna Newco., a venture between the traditional owners and Numa Numa that will manage the lawsuit and seek to redevelop the mine, according to the statement.

See also: Copper falls below US$12,000 in London as metals turmoil deepens

Lloyds, an Indian iron ore miner, was selected by the ABG as a development partner for Panguna after private negotiations saw the firm beat out China’s CMOC Group Ltd last year.

title: StarHub targets savings from proposed M1 merger, plans to retain brands
article:
StarHub is targeting $110 million in annual cost savings from its proposed combination with M1, while management plans to keep customer prices stable during 2027 as the businesses come together.

The merger savings are expected to reach their full annual run rate by FY2030, with an estimated net present value of $1.1 billion. They would add to $70 million of reductions already planned by StarHub and $40 million by M1, taking total annual cost savings to $220 million once fully realised.

StarHub will issue approximately 651.7 million new shares to M1’s shareholders, representing approximately 27.4% of its enlarged share capital. Keppel will hold an effective 23% interest in the enlarged group, with the remaining 4.4% held by M1’s other shareholders.

StarHub has also exercised an option to acquire Circles.Life’s Singapore mobile business, with completion anticipated alongside the M1 transaction.

At a Nov 24 briefing, StarHub CEO-designate Matt Williams outlined cost overlaps across StarHub and M1’s networks, IT, commercial functions and operations, including nearby mobile sites. The integration plan also includes retiring duplicate IT systems, consolidating supplier contracts, rationalising the retail footprint and sharing customer service platforms and facilities, alongside greater use of automation and AI.

See also: StarHub to pay $677.7 mil for M1 in all-share deal; to acquire Circles Life too

The merger savings estimate is net of integration costs, according to Williams. Realising those savings will take time as the companies integrate their infrastructure, with StarHub CFO Jacky Lo expecting them to build from 2029 onwards. In the meantime, StarHub aims to complete its separate cost programme by 2028.

StarHub’s proposed merger with M1 would also give it full ownership of Antina, their equally owned joint venture that builds and operates shared parts of their 5G mobile networks.

“[This move will allow us to] move faster, more aggressively, consolidate more network assets, drive more network efficiencies, improve quality, and reduce cost, albeit over time,” says StarHub CEO Nikhil Eapen, adding that potential capital expenditure synergies are still being assessed and have yet to be quantified.

See also: CrowdStrike reaches US$44 bil cyber deal to acquire Zscaler

Revenue gains are also excluded from the estimates because they depend on market developments, according to Williams. His immediate priority is to leave customers undisturbed during integration. “Our intention is not to make changes during 2027 because our focus during that year is really on making sure that we bring the businesses together,” he says.

The planned additions of M1 and Circles.Life follow StarHub’s full acquisition of MyRepublic Broadband and purchase of MyRepublic Mobile. The operator has also migrated redONE subscribers to its Eight brand. Eapen describes StarHub as the “market consolidator” and credits its acquisitions with having “repositioned the market landscape”.

Within the enlarged group, Williams plans to continue StarHub’s “multi-segment, multi-brand approach”. The portfolio would span full-service brands StarHub and M1; digital and specialist offerings including Giga, Circles.Life and MyRepublic; and value brands Eight and Maxx.

“Each of those brands is very carefully and deliberately targeted at a segment of customers”, he says. He points to customers choosing to spend more at StarHub and Eight, attributing this to offering the brand, pricing and experience they wanted. Dedicated teams serving MyRepublic, Eight and Giga would therefore continue, with a similar approach planned for Circles.Life. There were no immediate plans to consolidate brands, although Williams left that possibility open.

On staffing, Williams remains focused on building the business, with no specific plan to cut jobs at present. However, staffing would be examined carefully as integration progressed. The combined workforce would number about 2,700.

To stay ahead of Singapore and the region’s corporate and economic trends, click here for Latest Section

Since Circles.Life already pays M1 a share of its revenue for network access, Eapen sees ownership as a way to secure that payment stream beyond the existing contract and bring the revenue Circles.Life retains into the group.

StarHub has not disclosed the price for Circles.Life. However, Williams shares that the agreed formula uses customer numbers and lifetime value, an approach typical for mobile virtual network operators. Eapen expects the acquisition to be “overall accretive to the package of transactions, [with a valuation multiple] slightly lower than the multiple of the combination with M1”.

For M1, StarHub and Keppel used roughly comparable enterprise value-to-ebitda multiples to arrive at what Eapen describes as a “fair transaction”. The all-share structure, he adds, would preserve the combined group’s “balance sheet capacity to invest and grow”.

At StarHub’s 15-day volume-weighted average share price of $1.04, the shares issued for the M1 transaction would be worth about $678 million. Adding $380 million of M1 net debt gives an enterprise value of $1.058 billion.

StarHub and Keppel’s higher $1.36 billion enterprise valuation for M1 is based on a modelled StarHub share value of $1.50, which incorporates the estimated operating savings.

When asked why StarHub’s valuation was below Simba’s earlier offer, Eapen calls the transactions “fundamentally different”, contrasting Simba’s cash offer with the proposed share-based combination. He also cites differences in timing, valuation and market dynamics. That equity participation makes Keppel a partner in integrating the businesses and delivering savings, adds Williams. “And as a result of that, my expectation is that Keppel will also benefit over time from the value that we create,” he says.

Keppel’s shares would be subject to a 12-month lock-up after completion, with any subsequent disposal undertaken in a measured and orderly manner, subject to market conditions. The intention is to grow and realise value rather than monetise the investment too quickly, says Eapen.

The enlarged group would serve more than 4.1 million mobile customers and more than 750,000 broadband customers, according to StarHub. Williams puts its combined share of mobile revenue at 41%.

Pro forma revenue for the 12 months ended June 2026 would be $2.601 billion and ebitda $511 million, compared with StarHub’s standalone $1.868 billion and $343 million.

Pro forma net debt would stand at 2.9 times ebitda, including Antina’s debt and the Circles.Life acquisition. Lo declines to provide a separate Antina debt figure. Management aims to bring leverage towards 2 to 2.5 times through cash generation and savings.

While integration proceeds, StarHub intends to maintain a distribution of six cents a share for existing shareholders in 2027, supported by operating cash flows and proceeds from the anticipated sale of its remaining stake in cybersecurity company Ensign InfoSecurity. Eapen expects a sale announcement soon, and says that Keppel has waived its right to those distributions.

StarHub plans to submit its regulatory application no later than Nov 25, with a public consultation expected soon afterwards, according to Eapen.

The M1 combination is expected to complete by 1HFY2027, subject to regulatory clearance, shareholder approvals at StarHub and Keppel, and other conditions. StarHub also plans to present its strategy for the enlarged business during that period.

title: Thai retail giant Central weighs first leader outside family
article:
(Nov 24): Central Group is considering appointing a leader from outside its founding Chirathivat family for the first time in its nearly 80-year history, as one of Thailand’s biggest conglomerates prepares for a new generation of leadership.

The retail and property empire, which owns businesses ranging from shopping malls and hotels in Thailand to some of Europe’s best-known luxury department stores, may no longer need to rely exclusively on family members to run it, chief executive officer Tos Chirathivat said. A rapidly changing business environment means Central needs the most capable person at the helm to ensure its long-term survival, he said.

“Many family businesses around the world don’t necessarily have family members as their leaders,” Tos told Thai media outlet Longtunman in an interview. “Ultimately, you need to choose the most capable and suitable person to run the business, supported by a strong board and good governance.”

Tos’s comments signal a potential shift in how one of Thailand’s most prominent family-controlled business groups approaches succession. Family conglomerates have long played an outsized role in the Southeast Asian country’s economy, with leadership typically passed from one generation to the next even as their businesses expand internationally.

Central has been led by members of the Chirathivat family since Tos’s grandfather, Tiang Chirathivat, founded the business in Bangkok in 1947. Bloomberg ranked the clan among Asia’s richest earlier this year.

The conglomerate has increasingly brought professional executives into senior management, while members of the Chirathivat family retain key leadership and board positions. Tos also serves as executive chairman and has played a major part in the group’s transformation into an international retail group.

See also: Indosuez Wealth Management and INSEAD prepare heirs to better manage family business

The group’s major listed companies include Central Pattana Pcl, Thailand’s largest shopping mall developer, and Central Retail Group, which operates department stores and hypermarkets in Thailand and Vietnam.

Its international expansion has accelerated in recent years, particularly in European luxury retail, with a portfolio of high-end department stores including Selfridges in the UK, Italy’s Rinascente and Germany’s KaDeWe. That business is facing some near-term challenges as geopolitical conflicts weigh on consumer sentiment and spending, Tos said, and Central is monitoring how long the weakness may persist.

title: Singapore won’t be conduit to skirt US chip curbs, PM says
article:
(Nov 24): Prime Minister Lawrence Wong doesn’t want Singapore to be used as a route for companies seeking to circumvent US chip export controls, as authorities in the city-state investigate locally based firm Megaspeed over its purchases of Nvidia Corp chips.

“We do not enforce America’s export controls, but we do not want Singapore to be used and abused as a conduit by companies to circumvent America’s export controls,” Wong said Tuesday during a visit to Australia. Singapore will facilitate US checks while taking “very firm enforcement actions” against companies that breach local law, he said.

The Commerce Department earlier put Megaspeed International on a US trade blacklist barring it from buying advanced artificial intelligence chips. The company is at the heart of the scandal that briefly cost Jensen Huang his job as Nvidia’s chief executive officer.

The move came soon after Nvidia’s board reinstated Huang as CEO following his ouster over reports of multiple affairs, including his admitted relationship with Alice Huang, a former Megaspeed executive suspected by the US of spying for China. Beijing has rejected the spying allegation as baseless.

The city-state said this month that it barred her from re-entering the country in February and gave her a “stern warning” after finding insufficient evidence to prosecute. The US government has been investigating whether Megaspeed has smuggled Nvidia chips into China.

Singapore began an independent probe in February 2025 into Megaspeed and several other firms over suspected false declarations involving server purchases and related offences. Wong reiterated Tuesday during a news conference with his Australian counterpart that the chips Megaspeed bought from Nvidia never entered Singapore and that investigations remain ongoing.

See also: Crowded Singapore bank stocks face rotation as AI risks mount

“We are continuing to have discussions with American authorities — where the end users are,” Wong said, adding that officials were also verifying various documents. “The chips were routed through Singapore to other countries and obviously we cannot investigate all that’s happening, you know, in these third countries,” he said.

Asked about Jensen Huang’s return as Nvidia CEO, he added, “Nvidia’s board will have to do what it needs to do. They have decided, so be it.”

Singapore was among nine US partners that recently signed a pledge with Washington to safeguard sensitive technologies and critical infrastructure, part of America’s broader “Pax Silica” initiative to counter China’s AI ambitions.

title: Hewlett Packard gives outlook that falls short of the most optimistic estimates
article:
(Nov 24): Hewlett Packard Enterprise Co gave a revenue forecast for the current quarter that fell short of the most optimistic estimates, disappointing some investors who were looking for a bigger boost from the artificial intelligence (AI) boom.

Sales will be US$14 billion ($18.1 billion) to US$14.6 billion in the period ending in January, while profit, excluding some items, is projected at US$1.30 to US$1.40 a share, the company said Monday in a statement. Analysts surveyed by Bloomberg, on average, expected profit of US$1.08 a share on revenue of US$12.8 billion. Sales estimates for the fiscal first quarter were as high as US$14.7 billion.

HPE’s results have been spurred by demand for AI work, which has accelerated construction of data centres and corporate networks that train and run models. That has raised investor expectations for growth.

The shares declined about 2% in extended trading after closing at US$48.31 in New York. The stock had doubled this year through the close.

The company sells AI servers with Nvidia Corp chips and is also seeing rising revenue from Advanced Micro Devices Inc-based machines, which also contain networking chips from HPE’s Juniper unit, chief executive officer Antonio Neri said in an interview.

“This is in many ways a completely different company than it was a year ago, driven by the innovation that we have across networking, cloud and AI, and it points also to the durability of the demand that we see in the market,” he said.

See also: Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO with government input

For the fiscal year beginning this month, HPE raised its outlook for sales to as high as US$63.1 billion and profit to as much as US$5.35 a share. The company’s revenue range represents an increase of 27% to 35%, above a previous forecast for 15% at the midpoint.

Neri also said the company is getting a better handle on supply shortages and price increases for key components like memory.

“We have a more stable understanding of cost, and we have established very scalable pricing actions that ultimately not only allows us to deal with the cost curves that we have seen, but also passing it to the market,” he said.

See also: China’s next AI deals clouded by selloff after Anthropic IPO

Fiscal fourth-quarter revenue jumped 50% to US$14.5 billion, compared with analysts’ average estimate of US$14.3 billion. Profit, excluding some items, was US$1.43 a share. Analysts, on average, projected US$1.28.

title: US Senate probes Vance role in Vitol choice for Venezuela oil
article:
(Nov 24): A US senator is investigating the role Vice President JD Vance played in awarding a lucrative Venezuelan oil contract to a political donor and then-executive at commodities trader Vitol Group.

Democratic Senator Maggie Hassan sent the letter to Vance on Monday after Reuters reported that he met with Vitol trader John Addison a week before the US invaded Venezuela and captured authoritarian leader Nicolas Maduro. Hassan is poised to chair the Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs.

“Given the significant financial interests at stake and the importance of safeguarding government decision-making against improper influence, I am seeking information about your involvement in these arrangements,” the letter said. “Your personal and political relationships with Mr Addison raise concerns about how Vitol may have obtained this opportunity.”

Vitol Group and Trafigura Group won special licences to ship still-sanctioned Venezuelan barrels shortly after Maduro’s downfall — giving them a head start in boosting the Opec member’s supply to international markets. Those deals helped drive a resurgence in Venezuela’s crude exports, helping to alleviate some of the tightness after the war in Iran hampered Persian Gulf supply.

Vance and Addison never discussed the sale of Venezuelan oil, a spokesperson for the vice president said. “This alleged meeting never happened, and it’s a shame that Reuters has allowed itself to be duped by an anonymous source peddling fiction as fact,” said Luke Schroeder, a Vance spokesman.

Vitol didn’t immediately respond to a request for comment. Bloomberg wasn’t immediately able to contact Addison, who retired from Vitol earlier this year.

See also: European gas surges as cold snap threatens tight inventories

As incoming chair of the Senate committee, Hassan asked Vance to provide any communications with Addison and Vitol related to Venezuelan oil since January 2025. She also asked what role Vance or his staff had in the administration’s decision to select Vitol to sell Venezuelan oil.

title: Gold extends gain after Nvidia’s rehiring of Huang sparks rally
article:
(Nov 24): Gold rose for a second day, after Jensen Huang’s surprise return to the helm of Nvidia Corp recharged bets on artificial intelligence and spurred rallies across markets.

Bullion climbed as much as 1% to near US$3,670 an ounce, after jumping 2.7% in the previous session. The rebound partially retraced last week’s near-9% drop that took the metal to the lowest in more than a year. Nvidia reinstated Huang as president and chief executive officer of the world’s largest chipmaker less than two weeks after he resigned under a cloud of scandal.

The announcement propelled Wall Street to its best day since April 2025, and helped spur a rebound in gold two weeks after the metal dropped below the US$4,000-an-ounce support level. An earlier rout in technology stocks had prompted investors to sell bullion to cover losses, adding to pressure from stubborn inflation and hawkish commentary from Federal Reserve (Fed) officials.

“Gold’s sharp rebound appears to reflect a sudden pivot in market sentiment after Huang’s return reignited risk appetite across markets,” said Hebe Chen, senior market analyst at Vantage Global Prime, adding that softer oil prices and an easing in longer-dated US Treasury yields were also supportive for bullion.

“However, it remains premature to call a bottom,” Chen added. “These supportive forces have yet to prove they can sustain more than a short-lived relief rally.”

Investors still expect monetary policy to remain tight in the coming months. Fed New York president John Williams said Monday that the central bank still has “work to do” to tame sticky inflation, and the market is pricing in another interest-hike rate at the Fed’s December meeting. Higher borrowing costs are typically negative for gold, which doesn’t pay interest.

See also: Gold rebounds as tech rout spurs shift to havens, Treasury rally

Elsewhere, the yellow metal received some support from Chinese gold imports, which surged to a record US$209 billion ($269.9 billion) so far this year in an unprecedented buying spree that’s helping to keep a lid on its trade surplus with major partners like the European Union.

Spot gold rose 0.6% to US$3,656.50 an ounce at 9.08am in Singapore. Silver was 1.1% higher at US$43.57 an ounce, after surging almost 5% on Monday. Platinum and palladium also advanced. The Bloomberg Dollar Spot Index, a gauge of the US currency, edged down 0.1% after rising 0.2% in the previous session to its highest since April 2025.

title: Asian stocks jump as Huang’s return lifts AI trade
article:
(Nov 24): Asian shares rallied as Jensen Huang’s return to lead Nvidia Corp revived enthusiasm for the artificial intelligence (AI) trade, helping the region’s major chipmakers rebound from last week’s rout.

MSCI Inc’s Asia Pacific equities index climbed 4.1%, set for its biggest gain in more than three months. Tuesday’s rally snapped an eight-day run of losses that pushed the gauge close to a bear market. Taiwan’s benchmark surged 9% in its largest advance since April 2025, while South Korea’s climbed more than 7% in its best day since July.

Samsung Electronics Co, SK Hynix Inc and Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co all surged more than 8%, helping boost a regional gauge of chip-related stocks by almost 10%.

The gains in Asia, where chip-related companies are seen as the picks and shovels of the AI buildout, came after Huang’s surprise return to Nvidia propelled Wall Street to its best day since April 2025. His comeback to the company at the centre of the AI boom restored confidence in technology stocks after his exit earlier this month threw the trade into turmoil and added to doubts over whether future profits can justify the industry’s surge in debt-financed spending.

“Jensen’s return to Nvidia as CEO is about re-instilling confidence back into the markets and into the broader AI ecosystem,” said Felix Wang, managing director of global technology at Hedgeye Risk Management. “Jensen’s voice in AI matters is unparalleled. With Jensen back in the saddle, the global server market may receive a boost.”

Elsewhere, Treasuries steadied and crude oil held its losses. Gold extended its gains to trade around US$3,660 an ounce.

See also: Asian stocks fall as Anthropic slips in after-hours

The global stock rally on Monday marked a dramatic reversal after the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average on Friday entered correction territory — defined as a decline of at least 10% from their recent high. The S&P 500 climbed 4.7% to snap a seven-day losing streak. The Nasdaq 100 surged 6.9%, pulling back from the brink of a bear market, while a gauge of semiconductor shares jumped 14%. Nvidia shares soared 31%, the most since 2003.

Nvidia’s board reinstated Huang after a series of meetings and input from “senior levels” of the government. US President Donald Trump praised the decision, saying the US has no reason to believe Huang “poses any risk” to national security.

“Investors are in a more cheery mood,” said Frederic Neumann, chief Asia economist at HSBC Holdings plc. “However, not all clouds overhanging the AI sector have parted. While Jensen’s leadership of Nvidia may reduce near-term risks around the company’s prospects, broader regulatory uncertainty remains in the US with respect to data centre build-out and technology transfers.”

See also: Stocks fluctuate after Anthropic IPO, copper gains

Moreover, tightening financial conditions still pose a powerful headwind for an industry increasingly reliant on debt to finance its investment, Neumann said.

For investors betting against Nvidia, Monday’s big rebound turned a lucrative wager into a financial wrecking ball.

As Nvidia surged, GraniteShares 2x Short NVDA Daily ETF (ticker NVD), which seeks to deliver twice the inverse of the chipmaker’s daily performance, plunged 63%.

Beyond AI, traders have plenty to parse this week, with the Thanksgiving holiday on Thursday in the US.

US data this week will help shape expectations for the Federal Reserve’s December meeting, with consumer confidence due Tuesday, followed Wednesday by the central bank’s preferred inflation gauge, consumer spending and revised third-quarter growth.

“It’s a nerve-wracking period to be long,” Carol Schleif, chief market strategist at BMO Wealth Management, said on Bloomberg Television. “But on the other hand, when you have a headline like you had today, it’s a nerve-wracking period to be out of the market too.”

title: Tan Chin Hwee joins IFM as Asia Credit adviser and member and Asia Debt Strategy investment committee chairman
article:
IFM Investors has appointed Tan Chin Hwee, the former Asia-Pacific CEO of Trafigura, as an adviser and member of its Asia Credit Investment Committee. He will also chair the investment committee for IFM's Asia Debt Strategy.

The appointment comes two months after the pension-owned global asset manager opened a Singapore office in September. The office is meant to help IFM originate, assess and execute deals locally, and to work more closely with businesses and partners in the region.

Tan has more than three decades of investment and business experience in Asia. He was previously a founding partner and co-head of Apollo Global Management's Asia-Pacific business. He is also chairman of Singapore Trade Data Exchange Services and of the Energy Supply Resilience Advisory Panel and chairperson of Salt Investments' newly-convened committee of strategic advisors

"We're delighted to be working with Chin Hwee, who brings deep private credit and investment expertise, extensive knowledge of markets across Asia and experience building and leading businesses in the region," says Hiran Wanigasekera, IFM's executive director and co-head of APAC diversified credit.

He adds that IFM is looking for investments that can deliver attractive risk-adjusted returns for its clients and grow the retirement savings of the working people they invest for.

IFM has already started deploying capital through its private credit activities in Asia. Investment director Lee Hong Ern says the firm sees further potential as the market develops, and that Tan's regional experience and relationships will be "particularly valuable" as it weighs investments across different markets.

See also: Karen Lee steps down as CEO of Alpha Integrated REIT; CFO steps up as CEO-Designate

Tan, who says he has invested in Asian private credit since 2003, said the market has kept evolving through cycles. "Asia continues to offer opportunities for private credit as businesses look beyond traditional sources of capital to support their growth," he said. He added that IFM brings a long-term approach and established experience in private markets.

IFM is owned by pension funds and invests across infrastructure equity and debt, private equity, private credit, real estate and listed equities. It manages about A$300 billion ($256.93 billion) as of Sept 30 and serves more than 900 institutional investors from 18 offices across Australia, Europe, North America and Asia.

title: Kin Global secures three new design and build contracts worth $10.4 mil
article:
Kin Global announced that its wholly-owned subsidiary, Kin Productions Pte Ltd, has secured three new design and build (D&B) contracts with a combined value of around $10.4 million.

Kin Global says that the above new contracts are expected to be completed in 2027 and barring any unforeseen circumstances, these will enhance its revenue visibility and contribute positively to its financial performance across the duration of the projects.

“These latest contract awards demonstrates the confidence our clients place in our capabilities and the growing international reach of our D&B business,” says Vincent Chai, executive director and CEO of Kin Global.

As at 9.08am, shares of Kin Global were trading flat at 14 cents.

title: StarHub to pay $677.7 mil for M1 in all-share deal; to acquire Circles Life too
article:
The long-awaited next chapter of the consolidation of Singapore's intensely competitive mobile industry is finally taking place.

Not only is StarHub buying M1 from Keppel, it is acquiring another smaller operator, Circles Life as well, the company says in separate announcements.

First, StarHub will pay Keppel and other M1 owners $677.7 million in an all-share deal, enlarging its share base by 651.7 million.

M1 comes with net debt of some $380 million, for a total enterprise value of around $1.1 billion.

In contrast, Simba's all-cash deal valued M1 at $1.43 billion before that was spiked by regulators in May this year.

Keppel will end up as a substantial StarHub shareholder with a stake of 23%, with other M1 shareholders holding another 4.4%.

See also: CrowdStrike reaches US$44 bil cyber deal to acquire Zscaler

Keppel will not sell its StarHub shares for at least a year.

This latest development in the local mobile industry comes after a month with StarHub's acquisition of MyRepublic's smallish mobile base of just some 85,000 active users.

In a separate announcement, StarHub says it has exercised its call option to acquire Circles.Life Singapore, the Singapore mobile business of Liberty Wireless.

title: US blacklists Megaspeed, and six firms across Malaysia, Singapore and Thailand over chip diversion risk
article:
(Nov 24): The US Commerce Department has put Megaspeed International Pte Ltd on a trade blacklist, with the Bureau of Industry and Security adding it to the Entity List in a final rule, citing a risk that the company could divert advanced computing items to unauthorised end users or uses.

The rule covers seven entities in total, spread across Malaysia, Singapore, and Thailand. Under Singapore, it lists Megaspeed International Pte. Ltd. (also known as 7Road International), Apex Enterprise Solutions (Singapore) Pte Ltd, and Swiftdata Pte. Ltd.

The Malaysian entries are MSFusion Sdn. Bhd., PT Megaspeed International, and Speedmatrix Sdn Bhd, while Megaspeed (Thailand) Co., Ltd. is the sole Thai listing, according to a document filed by the department on Monday.

"These entities have been determined by the U.S. Government to be acting contrary to the national security or foreign policy interests of the United States," read the summary of the document.

The government says the additions reflect a significant risk that these entities could divert advanced computing commodities to unauthorized end uses or end users.

Each entity now faces a license requirement for all items subject to the Export Administration Regulations(EAR), and applications will be reviewed under a presumption of denial.

See also: Asian stocks to rally as Huang’s return revives AI

This latest restriction by Washington came after a probe on Megaspeed over chip exports, with Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent reportedly saying several agencies had backed blacklisting the company for months before any decision was made.

Megaspeed, a cloud computing firm and Nvidia partner, was suspected of funneling restricted AI chips into China, and it has been closely tied to an espionage investigation involving Nvidia.

The decision, according to the directive filed on Monday by Commerce, was made by the end-user review committee, which includes Commerce (as chair), State, Defense, Energy, and, where appropriate, Treasury, and it adds entries by majority vote.

See also: Stocks jump most since April 2025 as Huang is back

A savings clause lets shipments already en route proceed under their prior eligibility if completed within 30 days of public inspection.

The rule was issued without prior notice and comment under the Export Control Reform Act of 2018, and it is treated as a national security function exempt from several regulatory requirements.

The document was signed by Deputy Assistant Secretary for Strategic Trade, Julia Khersonsky, filed on Nov. 23, 2026, and is scheduled for publication in the Federal Register on Nov. 25, 2026.

title: Singapore raises 2026 GDP growth estimate to around 6%; expects some easing in 2027
article:
The government is projecting Singapore's economy to grow by around 6% this year, an upgrade from an earlier estimate of between 4.5 to 5.5%.

However, for the coming 2027, growth is likely to ease to between 2.5 to 4.5%.

According to the Ministry of Energy, Trade and Industry (METI), Singapore grew 6.1% y-o-y in 3Q, led by wholesale trade, manufacturing and finance & insurance sectors.

This growth rate is a tad below 6.4% seen in the preceding 2Q.

On a q-on-q seasonally-adjusted basis, the economy expanded by 1.5%, moderating from the 1.8% in 2Q.

For the first three quarters of 2026, Singapore’s GDP grew 6.2% year-on-year.

See also: Singapore core inflation eases to 1.5%, giving MAS room to pause

METI last upgraded its forecast for 2026 in August to 4.5 to 5.5% as the economic impact of the Middle East conflict was less severe than initially projected, while the global AI investment boom was expected to provide significant tailwinds to growth.

"Since then, AI-related production and exports, driven by stronger-than-expected buildout of data centres, have continued to accelerate. The momentum is expected to continue for the rest of the year," says METI.

The ministry notes that energy prices have contributed to global inflationary pressures and tighter monetary policy in several economies, but on balance, Singapore’s external demand outlook for the year has improved compared to the assessment in August.

See also: Singapore’s next phase of growth: Harnessing AI to sustain competitiveness

"Strong global AI-related demand will continue to drive growth in the manufacturing and wholesale trade sectors, while growth in outward-oriented services sectors such as finance & insurance and information & communications should remain resilient," says METI.

This coming 2027, METI expects oil supply from the Middle East to recover gradually, supported in part by the increased use of alternative transport routes such as pipelines within the Gulf.

"This should lead to easing global energy prices and hence inflationary pressures over the course of the year," says METI.

On the other hand, the pace of growth in new AI investments is expected to moderate from its high level in 2026.

In view of these factors, GDP growth in most of Singapore’s key trading partners is projected to soften in 2027.

In the US, for one, growth is expected to ease as restrictive monetary policy and weaker real wage growth weigh on investment and consumption, while the pace of AI investments is projected to ease.

China’s economy is also expected to slow as export growth softens amidst moderating global AI-related demand and sluggish consumption growth.

The Asean region too will ease as the pace of expansion in both AI investments and AI-related exports moderate from their high levels in 2026.

METI warns that concerns about the sustainability of the global AI cycle could trigger sharper corrections in global financial markets, with potential spillovers to broader economic activity.

Also, further escalation of the conflict in the Middle East could lead to fresh spikes in the price of energy commodities and therefore inflationary pressures.

Third, economic and political uncertainties in external economies could weigh on investment and consumption in these economies.

Against this backdrop, Singapore’s GDP growth is projected to moderate in 2027.

Growth enjoyed by the electronics and precision engineering clusters of the manufacturing sector, for one, may moderate from the high levels recorded in 2026.

title: Stocks jump most since April 2025 as Huang is back
article:
(Nov 25) : An overnight bounce in stocks erupted into the biggest rally since April 2025 after Nvidia Corp.’s reinstatement of Jensen Huang as chief executive officer recharged artificial-intelligence bets.

Shares of the giant chipmaker soared 31%, the most since 2003. Just days earlier, the firm had been at the center of a rout that brought the Nasdaq 100 to the brink of a bear market. The tech-heavy gauge climbed 6.9%. The S&P 500 rose 4.7%. A measure of semiconductor powerhouses jumped 14%.

Nvidia’s board reinstated Huang after a series of meetings and input from “senior levels” of the government. President Donald Trump praised the decision, saying the US has no reason to believe it “poses any risk” to national security.

Huang’s ouster after admitting extramarital affairs had thrown the AI trade into crisis, raising concern about the company at the center of the boom that has fueled big swaths of the economy.

“The reinstatement of the prolific leader of Nvidia’s AI buildout as CEO is bolstering confidence that the momentum of modern technology will remain robust, while sidelining fears of a slowdown,” according to Jose Torres at Interactive Brokers.

Huang returned to the company’s Santa Clara, California office on Monday to applause and cheers from employees who shared videos. He spoke with them briefly at one of the entrances.

See also: Asia’s stock rescue efforts gather pace after Wall Street plunge

While Nvidia’s near-term business fundamentals are the same with or without Huang, it is a fundamentally different stock with him at the helm, according to Joe Tigay at Equity Armor Investments.

“Huang has been an instrumental hype-man, dealmaker, powerbroker, financier and executive for the industry, supporting its expansion and shoring up optimism whenever doubts about massive capital expenditures, uncertain payback prospects and/or integration capabilities surfaced,” said Torres at Interactive Brokers.

His return helps remove a key level of uncertainty around the AI trade, noted Glen Smith at GDS Wealth Management.

See also: Dip buyers hesitate to step in as Nasdaq 100 nears a bear market

“It appears the worst is over and the company can move on from this,” he added. “Corrections can sometimes end as quickly as they begin and we believe the bottom in stocks is likely in.”

title: US stocks soar as Huang’s Nvidia return fuels AI bets
article:

Shares of the giant chipmaker soared 34%, the biggest advance since 2000. A closely watched gauge of semiconductor powerhouses jumped 14%. The S&P 500 rose 5%. The Nasdaq 100 climbed 7%.

Nvidia’s board reinstated Huang after a series of meetings and input from “senior levels of the United States government”. President Donald Trump praised the decision, saying the US has no reason to believe it “poses any risk” to national security.

Huang’s ouster after admitting extramarital affairs had thrown the AI trade into crisis, raising concern about the company at the centre of the boom that has fuelled big swaths of the economy.

“Nvidia’s earnings and near-term business fundamentals are the same with or without Jensen Huang,” said Joe Tigay at Equity Armor Investments. “But as an investment, Nvidia is a fundamentally different stock with Jensen at the helm.”

The decision helps remove a key level of uncertainty from the AI trade, according to Glen Smith at GDS Wealth Management.

See also: Nasdaq 100 has worst week since 2020 on AI drama

“It appears that the worst is over and the company can move on from this,” he said. “Stock market corrections can sometimes end as quickly as they begin and we believe the bottom in stocks is likely in.”

Even before Nvidia’s statement, Morgan Stanley’s Michael Wilson said earnings and valuations were both supportive of a market rebound.

“This is the fat pitch we have patiently been waiting for, and we’re not going to miss it,” he wrote. “Markets bottom on bad news and deleveraging. We have had a lot of both.”
